metadata.author: Texas Probate Real Estate
metadata.shortDescription:
Probate attorney Nancy Perry Eaton (Law Office of Nancy Perry Eaton) and Jeremy Kritt explain Texas probate pitfalls: affidavits of heirship, AI errors and investor risks.

CHAPTERS

02:42 Understanding the Probate Process

07:42 The Role of Title Companies
10:18 The Impact of AI on Legal Practices
12:56 Cautionary Tales in Probate Transactions
15:23 Navigating Real Estate Transactions in Probate
17:48 Legal Implications of Improper Sales
20:33 Conclusion and Key Takeaways
23:16 Navigating Knowledge in Law and Real Estate
25:21 The Importance of Expertise in Probate Real Estate
30:57 Building Trust and Relationships in Real Estate
35:45 Advice for Personal Representatives and Executors
39:38 Demystifying the Probate Process

GUEST
Nancy Eaton, Esq., Law Office of Nancy Perry Eaton, PLLC
Website: https://www.perryeatonlaw.com/

ABOUT THIS VIDEO
In this episode of the Texas Probate Real Estate Podcast, host Jeremy Kritt sits down with award‑winning probate attorney Nancy Perry Eaton to unpack the real‑world challenges Texas families face when dealing with probate, affidavits of heirship, title issues, and investor pressure. Nancy, voted Best Attorney and Best Law Firm in the Killeen Daily Herald’s Best of Central Texas (2025), explains why Texas title companies are rejecting affidavits of heirship more frequently and how missing heirs, inaccurate affidavits, or investor‑driven contracts can jeopardize title and expose families to legal risk.

Jeremy and Nancy explain the risks of signing contracts before an executor or administrator is officially appointed, the tactics wholesalers and “We Buy Houses” companies use to pressure grieving families, and the red flags heirs should watch for. They also cover why DIY probate, online templates, and AI‑generated legal documents often lead to costly mistakes, outline the differences between independent and dependent administrations, and show how attorneys and real estate professionals work together to protect the estate’s equity.

TAKEAWAYS
-AI cannot replace professional judgment built from years of legal and real estate experience.
-DIY probate filings are risky, especially when people misunderstand statutes or court procedures.
-Some agents sign listings before an executor is appointed, creating legal exposure for the estate.
-Many agents lack probate‑specific knowledge, including authority and title requirements.
-Probate real estate requires specialized expertise, not generic real estate experience.
-Investors and wholesalers often push unauthorized deals, causing long‑term title and heirship issues.
-Experienced attorneys and brokers understand the landmines and protect the estate from costly mistakes.
